issuers.name: Remora Markets
issuers.governanceEvidence: Every rToken mint names the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as mint, freeze, pause, permanent-delegate and metadata authority (RPC getAccountInfo on FJug3z58gssSTDhVNkTse5fP8GRZzuidf9SRtfB2RhDe and the other mints, 2026-09-16; re-verified 2026-09-17). Characterised 2026-09-17: that key is NOT a bare keypair but the Squads v4 vault PDA (vault index 0, bump 251) of multisig 7QsgDVkiM2285Mvi5TUf1gtHj1QzcqMyix6Rgrcqko35, which is owned by the Squads v4 program SQDS4ep65T869zMMBKyuUq6aD6EgTu8psMjkvj52pCf, has threshold 2 of 3 members, timeLock 0 and configAuthority 11111111111111111111111111111111 (no config authority, so membership and threshold are immutable), and had reached transactionIndex 640. Members: 4aog1ZhoEDrx47fddZ1BYq6yeXgb8mufTubJ3dvgLi6f (permissions 3), 7bzfFK9VxtUgK9Pr1mg7HegQtWPk9mXxmXkf556QMAEz (permissions 7), H61gpHmkSvTSLNWDuJvLA62EVtjrdfHDD5hF978pwa4E (permissions 6). Proof it is the vault and not a keypair: in tx 3wLDeSocn6Tg52KPjH3HWvohfpq9vVWoo8d9zXGLiSXd9L1h2BkpJtvYuET8KjurUuNMT1Ls1QEhRhrgsdGHy7Ts (2026-06-29) the Squads program logs 'Instruction: VaultTransactionExecute' and DQSTm2Wt... signs an inner SPL transferChecked as authority, which a transaction-level keypair signature does not do and a PDA can only do by CPI; the vault PDA derivation for index 0 also hashes to that address exactly. So all three powers sit behind a 2-of-3 multisig rather than one key, though the three member identities remain unattributed. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb on all five rStock mints — the same single address that holds mint, freeze and permanent delegate — so it inherits their characterisation. Multiplier 1 everywhere: never used. RESOLVED 2026-09-18: the doubt raised on 2026-09-17 — that DQSTm2Wt... reads as a plain system-owned account (owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, space 0) holding 0.001995004 SOL, i.e. the shape of a hot key — does not survive the transaction evidence, and a system-owned zero-space account is also exactly what an uninitialised Squads v4 vault PDA looks like. Re-read 2026-09-18: multisig 7QsgDVkiM2285Mvi5TUf1gtHj1QzcqMyix6Rgrcqko35 is still owned by the Squads v4 program and 495 bytes long, and in tx 3wLDeSocn6Tg52KPjH3HWvohfpq9vVWoo8d9zXGLiSXd9L1h2BkpJtvYuET8KjurUuNMT1Ls1QEhRhrgsdGHy7Ts (2026-06-29T09:35:46Z) the ONLY transaction signer is member H61gpHmkSvTSLNWDuJvLA62EVtjrdfHDD5hF978pwa4E, the Squads program logs 'Instruction: VaultTransactionExecute', DQSTm2Wt... appears as a non-signer writable account, and the inner spl-token transferChecked names DQSTm2Wt... as its 'authority' — which a non-signing account can only be by PDA CPI. The multisig reading stands; the flag is cleared. What remains unknown is who the three members are.

issuers.name: Republic Mirror
issuers.governanceEvidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key. keyGovernance.rebase is 'unknown' for the same single reason as the other three: no mint address is published, so no scaledUiAmountConfig extension — and therefore no rebase authority, and not even whether the extension exists — could be read from Solana mainnet. On paper, no programme document reserves a power to move or freeze a holder's tokens: the Private Placement Risk Disclosure says "The loss of one or more of such private keys will result in the loss of the holder’s digital Securities.", the rSPAX offering page restricts transfers only contractually, and the Terms of Service say of the Republic Wallet "At no time will we be able to access or transfer your funds without your consent." That leaves the clawback in Republic's description of its token standard unreconciled with its own offering documents until a mint can be read.

issuers.name: Shift leveraged tokens
issuers.governanceEvidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is the same per-mint key that already holds mint, freeze, pause, metadata and permanent delegate — eight distinct keys, one per mint — so it inherits their 'hot-key' characterisation. The mechanism is in use, not merely armed: SOX3S (authority 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA) reads a multiplier of 0.1, so a displayed SOX3S balance is already one tenth of its raw amount.

issuers.governanceEvidence: stocks/findings.md (Multisig evidence, 2026-09-16): the freeze key 7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o is a nonce-based hot key with no Squads program in its history and has exercised freeze/thaw four times. The mints carry no permanentDelegate at all, so there is no delegate authority to govern. keyGovernance.rebase is 'none': no scaledUiAmountConfig extension exists on any of the three T-Token mints (the extension list is transferFeeConfig, metadataPointer and tokenMetadata only), so there is no rebase authority to hold and no holder balance can be restated. That is an absence of capability, not an absence of research — Tessera is the only programme here that cannot re-denominate its holders.

finding.statement: The freeze key has 2 freezeAccount and 2 thawAccount transactions, all on 2026-06-07 and all on the T-SpaceX mint: 2grbfzkjwfEB1Em26Hfs1iYfoJEEmezvw9TSU1NNSVzF frozen 08:08:50Z and thawed 08:11:16Z, 6b99iGSCyivPVxztDLwMvpf2SvN22QJ4r5mGGe6t7RmN frozen 08:18:32Z and thawed 08:19:32Z. The power has been used on real holder accounts, not merely reserved - but the shape fits the published explanation rather than a compliance or dispute freeze: the key was funded 2026-06-01T12:51:58Z, the day Tessera's Hypernative threat-monitoring layer went live with "automated protective response", and each freeze was reversed within one to three minutes, which is what "recovery is deliberately manual" looks like when the investigation clears. Those five transactions are the key's entire history. What remains unmitigated: the Terms state no grounds, no notice, no time limit and no appeal, the docs' own Authorities & Security table omits the key, and no multisig program appears in any of its transactions.
Each mint carries transferFeeConfig at 20 bps with an unbounded maximum fee, so every secondary transfer is taxed at the token level.
